solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disagreement I have about iffy clue involving guesswork

indicators.note: the quarrel word and the contraction sit around the reworked letters

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
contracted, I have becomes I've

indicators.note: iffy means dubious or unsound, so the letters of clue are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A solver argues over a dodgy clue that relies on guessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iffy' looks like a comment on the clue's quality, but it shuffles 'clue' into ECUL; 'about' wraps the quarrel word round it, with the I've contraction at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculation is conjecture without firm evidence, so a speculative claim rests on guesses.

clue.text: Shame envelops cleric, to involve bringing bishop in, which means it can be stopped?

definitions.text: which means it can be stopped?

indicators.note: envelops means the word for shame wraps around everything else

parts.note: 'what a pity' and 'what a shame' mean the same
Rev, the Reverend, is a title for a cleric

indicators.note: bringing ... in means the letter for the bishop is placed inside the word for involve
together with bringing, says the bishop letter goes into the involve word

parts.note: to entail something is to involve it
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A long-winded question about a scandal surrounding a priest, which a bishop might halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop letter sits inside 'entail' to give ENTABIL. The question mark admits the definition is loose: the answer is the quality of being stoppable, phrased as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be stopped has the quality of being avoidable, the noun form of avoidable.

clue.text: Be disgustingly rich or modest about pounds?

indicators.note: about means the word for modest goes around the letter

parts.note: coy means shy or modest
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A question of whether to flaunt wealth or keep quiet about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rich' suggests wealth, but it means food too heavy and sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly sweet, rich food sickens with excess, which is to cloy.

clue.text: Switch starters of grapes, for example, and smoked salmon in such a package?

indicators.note: switch starters means the opening letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: grapes grow and are sold in a bunch
lox is cured or smoked salmon, as served with bagels

explanation.surface: Packing grapes and smoked salmon for a packed meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of BUNCH and LOX gives the answer; 'such' points back to the food in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A box holding a midday meal of grapes and lox is exactly that kind of container.

clue.text: Short cut to check support, …

indicators.note: short means the word is missing its last letter

parts.note: to trim is to cut
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: A brief trim to examine a support, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue with 6 down, whose 'its' refers back to this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged stand for a hot pot or kettle is a support.

clue.text: … its bottom half worn by son as underwear

indicators.note: worn by means the half word is wrapped around the son's letter
in a down answer the bottom half is the last three of its six letters

parts.note: its refers to the answer to the previous clue, 5 down

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a support's lower part worn by a boy as undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: VET, the last half of 5 down, goes round S. In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet worn beneath a shirt is a British undergarment.

clue.text: Underwear shot not seen in album

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lingerie photos left out of a photo album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a photograph in this album, but signals the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A coy, jokey term for underclothes: items too indelicate to mention.

clue.text: Frequently used lines in alcohol-serving bar hangout

indicators.note: in means the lines go inside the word for alcohol-serving

parts.note: a wet area or town allows alcohol to be sold, as opposed to dry
L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them stand for lines
a rod is a bar of metal or wood
a den is a favourite haunt or hangout

explanation.surface: Busy queues inside a pub serving drink, a popular haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' wants to be the pub, but it is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A path many feet have walked is much travelled, so it is regularly used.

clue.text: Initial survey represented E Asian concerns

indicators.note: represented in the sense of presented again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An opening study set out the worries of East Asian countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnoitring is exploring ground before action, a preliminary survey of the territory.

clue.text: PM's too depraved in vulgar, degrading place

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for vulgar

parts.note: cheap means tawdry or vulgar

indicators.note: depraved means corrupted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A prime minister so corrupt that they end up in a sleazy, debased setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depraved' shuffles the letters of 'PM's too' into OMPOST. 'degrading' is a pun: organic matter degrades, rotting down, in this pile.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden waste piled up to rot down is a spot where matter decays, a pun on degrading.

clue.text: To be yielding, somewhat?

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so only part of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: A question about whether being yielding counts as half-hearted submission.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'To be yielding', and the whole clue also defines: to comply is to be yielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Complying with orders is being yielding or submissive to authority.

clue.text: Prime Suspect: watch Inspector solve crime in the end

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of each of the five words that follow Prime

explanation.surface: Instructions to watch the TV drama Prime Suspect, where the inspector cracks the case at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime Suspect' looks like the TV series title, but 'Prime' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The number after two is divisible only by itself and one, making it a prime number.

clue.text: Audibly cross, weakly cry

indicators.note: audibly signals that a word's sound, not its spelling, is wanted

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone noticeably angry, crying feebly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the noun: a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To whimper or whine faintly, as a baby or kitten does, is to give a feeble cry.

clue.text: Camp can remove Erica from Essex town

indicators.note: remove ... from means the girl's name is taken out of the town
together with remove, says the name comes out of the town

parts.note: Billericay is a town in Essex, the county east of London

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a woman called Erica away from a commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' may suggest flamboyance, but it means a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal pot for boiling water over a campfire, shortened to its first part.

clue.text: Deer raised around old ruminants

indicators.note: around means the turned word goes about the letter
raised in a down answer means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: Deer reared alongside elderly cud-chewing animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns STAG into GATS, which goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cud-chewing farm animals such as nannies and billies are ruminants.

clue.text: Quibble as lawyers try suit, backtracking after peevishness

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece following the sulk word

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or peevishness

indicators.note: backtracking means the words for try and suit are read in reverse order and direction

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
to fit is to suit

explanation.surface: Legal people argue over a case, going back over it irritably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' turns GOFIT into TIFOG, and 'after' puts it behind PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Pettifogging is petty legal quibbling, the habit of a minor, fussy attorney.

clue.text: Ordinary guy runs to grab case for tablet or notebook

indicators.note: to grab means the man's name holds the outer letters inside it

parts.note: Joe, as in Joe Public or Joe Bloggs, is the average man

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, here the first and last of tablet

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An average bloke hurries to snatch a cover for his tablet computer or laptop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablet or notebook' suggest computers; the definition is the paper kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pad or exercise book for jotting notes down is a type of notebook.

clue.text: Grass-covered sort of fife: it may produce a buzz

indicators.note: covered means the grass word goes over the jumbled letters

parts.note: cane is a tall grass, such as sugar cane

indicators.note: sort of means a version of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fife wrapped in grass that hums when played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' shuffles 'fife' into FFEI. The buzz is not a fife's sound but the lift from a strong coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: The stimulant in coffee gives a jolt of energy, slang a buzz.

clue.text: Discriminatory underlease with termination brought forward

indicators.note: the word's final letter is moved one place earlier

parts.note: a sublet is an underlease, a lease granted by a tenant

explanation.surface: A sublease agreement with an early end date, described as biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'termination brought forward' looks like a contract term, but moves the last letter of SUBLET before L.
explanation.definitionFit: Discriminatory here means showing fine discernment, able to tell small differences apart, which is being subtle.

clue.text: Delivery from rapid server's backed-up function, frequently not quite secure

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to make something fast is to secure it

indicators.note: backed-up means the words for function and frequently are read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
oft is an old word for often or frequently

explanation.surface: A tennis server's delivery is backed up by a function that is not entirely safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed-up' gives TFOOD from the party and often words. The server is not a tennis player but a counter worker handing over a quick meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway burger handed over the counter is a meal served quickly.

clue.text: Drive most of young people to stop drinking

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is cut

parts.note: youth means young people collectively

explanation.surface: Steering teenagers away from alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up alcohol, often in a clinic, is to quit drinking.

clue.text: Shrublike, regularly pruned to expose clod

indicators.note: regularly pruned means every other letter is cut away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A shrub-like plant trimmed at intervals to reveal a lump of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clod' looks like soil in this garden scene; it means an oaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A big clumsy person, a lumbering lout, is a clod.

clue.text: Churlish nonsense involving Republican

indicators.note: involving means the word for nonsense wraps around the letter

parts.note: guff is empty talk or nonsense

explanation.surface: Rude rubbish spouted by a Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone rough, surly and bad-tempered in manner.

clue.text: North-eastern state absorbing south-western one causes confusion

indicators.note: absorbing means the first state's letters take in the second's

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware, on the US east coast
AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona

explanation.surface: One US state swallowing another creates chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunned, bewildered state is a kind of confusion.

clue.text: Self-importance of humourless house-sitter

parts.note: po, as in po-faced, means stern and humourless
an MP sits in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: The arrogance of a dour person minding someone's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house-sitter' reads as a home minder but is a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous display and ceremonious self-importance share the sense of showy grandeur.

clue.text: Sickly daughter that may be shaken for a spell

definitions.text: that may be shaken for a spell

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: A frail girl who might be shaken for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like a period of time, but it is magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's stick is waved to cast an enchantment.

clue.text: When score includes backing or lack of amplification at a high level?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: includes means the score word has the other pieces placed inside it

parts.note: a tally is a score or running count

indicators.note: backing means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round
no can mean without or lacking, as in 'no money'
a mic, a microphone, amplifies sound

explanation.surface: A musical question: whether a score has accompaniment or is played without a microphone, and at what volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives RO from 'or'. 'Score' and 'amplification' suggest music, but the score is a tally and 'lack of' simply means no.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugely, enormously, at a level as high as the stars; the question mark flags the pun on star-gazing.

clue.text: Special belt up to replace sides of modern trouser guard

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word for modern are dropped so that the other pieces stand in their place

parts.note: latter-day means of recent times, modern
belt up means be quiet, and sh is the hush command

explanation.surface: An order to fasten a special belt to swap the sides of a modern trouser protector.
explanation.walkthrough: SP and SH replace L and Y, the ends of LATTER-DAY. A spatterdash was a long legging worn to keep mud off trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned gaiter protected the legs and trousers from splashes of mud while riding.
